builds: Client host/core, integrated server, admin module, raid controls, Quickhacks, standalone crash monitor and installer passed.

checks.hostSafety: Passed background preparation, transaction deferral, paused failed initialization, manual rollback, repaired replacement, five controlled error simulations, deadline compensation, unsafe-unload refusal.

manualChecks: Actual armored train departure and timetable changes
Full-body native ricochet visuals and behavior
Map time of day on a new raid
Diplomatic immunity against Scavs and bosses
Frame-rate outcome and performance attribution during a real raid
In-game fatal overlay and completed native survived settlement
limitations: Compilation and isolated native-server tests do not establish in-raid behavior.
A managed load/init failure can be rolled back after successful cleanup; unsafe cleanup requires restarting.
After a native process crash, the independent monitor can show an error and export logs, but cannot perform in-game settlement.
Equipment rescue snapshots are durable backups; the UI does not equate a backup receipt or an extraction request with a completed server settlement.
Performance snapshots measure Assistant callback CPU time; they cannot independently attribute the engine, other mods or GPU costs.
